audit_scope.description: These subgraphs primarily cover CL logic (Fulu fork transition, proposer lookahead EIP-7917, blob schedule EIP-7892, fork digest separation) with one EL-touching component (EIP-7918 blob base fee reserve price modifying calc_excess_blob_gas).

in_scope: Block Validation (excess_blob_gas with reserve price, EIP-7918)

out_of_scope_reasons.JSON-RPC API: Explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty — vulnerabilities requiring publicly exposed API
out_of_scope_reasons.Beacon API: Explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty — vulnerabilities requiring publicly exposed API
out_of_scope_reasons.Infrastructure bugs: Webpages, DNS, email etc. are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.High-effort DoS: Sustained, CPU or bandwidth intensive, requires more than 1 packet or on-chain transaction
out_of_scope_reasons.Non-Fusaka vulnerabilities: Should be submitted via the standard Ethereum Foundation Bug Bounty Program

misclassified_entities.reason: Block Proposer in SUBGRAPH-FULU-BLOB-SCHEDULE is a local validator role, not an external entity. The proposer is part of the CL system itself. The actual external data source is the P2P network delivering blocks from proposers.

Block Producer in SUBGRAPH-EIP7918-RESERVE-PRICE is an internal role (the local node or a validator). The block production logic is internal to the EL. External threat comes from peers delivering blocks with crafted excess_blob_gas values.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via CL P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (beacon_block topic) and request-response (BlocksByRange, BlocksByRoot)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary beacon blocks, including blocks with malicious blob commitment counts, invalid execution payloads, or crafted fork digests. All P2P input must be fully validated. Covers EXT-PEER-NODE, EXT-REMOTE-PEER, and EXT-PEER from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL-CL communication is authenticated via JWT and co-located. However, data returned by EL (e.g., payload validity status, blob data) may not be fully re-verified by CL. A buggy or compromised EL could return incorrect validation results or corrupted data. Covers EXT-EXECUTION-LAYER from source subgraph.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL sends execution payloads to EL for validation. Authenticated via JWT but payload content (including excess_blob_gas in EIP-7918 context) must be independently validated by EL against parent block state.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via EL P2P Network (devp2p/eth/69)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth protocol (NewBlock, NewPooledTransactionHashes, BlockHeaders, BlockBodies)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL P2P peers are unauthenticated. They can send blocks with crafted excess_blob_gas values that exploit the EIP-7918 reserve price calculation. All block header fields must be independently recalculated and verified.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: A validator can propose blocks with maximum blob commitments at the dynamic limit boundary, attempt to exploit fork digest computation edge cases during blob schedule transitions, or submit conflicting attestations. Validator identity does not confer trust for data content.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV-Boost Relay / External Block Builder
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External relays provide execution payloads and blob bundles. They are unauthenticated third parties who could provide payloads crafted to exploit EIP-7918 reserve price edge cases or EIP-7892 blob limit boundary conditions.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P gossip beacon_block topic / BlocksByRange RPC
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: verify blob_kzg_commitments count against dynamic max_blobs_per_block from get_blob_parameters(epoch) per EIP-7892; verify execution payload via Engine API; verify proposer index against proposer_lookahead per EIP-7917; verify fork digest includes blob parameter hash.

Fork digest must be verified to include blob parameter hash (EIP-7892). Peers with mismatching fork digests (different blob schedules) must be rejected at connection time to prevent network partition attacks.

CL relies on EL to correctly validate execution payload state transitions including the modified calc_excess_blob_gas from EIP-7918. A buggy EL returning VALID for an invalid payload would cause CL to accept an invalid block. CL should verify blob commitment count independently (it does via process_execution_payload).

EL must independently recalculate excess_blob_gas using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas (EIP-7918 reserve price logic) from parent block state. Must not trust the header value provided — must recompute and compare. Must apply correct blobSchedule parameters for the fork epoch.

EL must fully validate all block header fields including excess_blob_gas (recalculated with EIP-7918 reserve price logic), blob_gas_used, and base_fee_per_gas. Must reject blocks where recalculated excess_blob_gas does not match header value.

Proposed blocks must pass full validation: proposer must match proposer_lookahead[slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH] per EIP-7917; blob commitments must not exceed dynamic limit per EIP-7892; execution payload must be verified via EL.

Execution payloads from relays must undergo the same full validation as any other block: blob commitment count check, Engine API verification with EIP-7918 reserve price logic, and proposer assignment verification.
